subject: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist
messages: From: Neha Kapoor To: Lauren Bishop , Vivek Kulkarni , Karthik Iyer , Monica Patel Date: Thu, 24 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700 Subject: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist Team — As we lock the QBR deck this week I want to consolidate the infra runway and unit-economics inputs. I attached the capacity model (v3) and a short experiments summary. High-level asks: 1) Confirm the GPU price deck / assumptions (per-GPU-hour, reserved vs spot mix). I used $2.40/hour as our base for A100-equivalent reserved — please flag if your region or partner pricing deviates. 2) Confirm utilization windows and the baseline steady-state slot utilization we should present (I currently have 62% global average with burst peaks at 88%). 3) Approve the proposed batching + prefix cache rollout plan for non-low-latency routes (details in the PDF). This leans heavier on batching for routes where 150–300ms added latency is acceptable. 4) Approve SLO risk posture: option A (conservative) vs option B (aggressive). Need a single recommendation for the leadership slide. Deadline: want final answers by EOD tomorrow (Fri) so Monica can produce the cost-sensitivity chart for the QBR. Attachments: [Attachment: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: batching_cache_experiments_summary.pdf (pdf)] Notes in the model: I included three scenarios — Base (current mix), Optimistic (higher batching + 10% more cache hit), and Conservative (lower batching due to latency concerns). Please annotate the model with your numeric changes rather than sending separate spreadsheets. Thanks — Neha Kapoor Director, Infrastructure Planning Redwood Inference neha_kapoor@redwood.com From: Vivek Kulkarni To: Neha Kapoor , Lauren Bishop Cc: Karthik Iyer , Monica Patel Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 09:44:12 -0700 Subject: Re: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist Neha — thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes after a pass through the model: - GPU price: FYI, committed discounts from our hyperscaler renewal landed last week — effective reserved A100-equivalent is $2.18/hr (I updated the "Committed" tab). Spot variance remains noisy; I kept 30% spot in Optimistic. - Utilization: the 62% steady-state looks right for v1 routes. For our heavy batch/multi-turn customers, utilization (after caching) trends to ~70%. I recommend using 65% as the QBR baseline to avoid overstating gains. - Batching/cache: the experiments PDF is good. For the rollout I propose: * Default batch size = 8 for non-rt routes; canary route set = top 5 revenue routes. * Cache TTL = 45s for prompt prefix caching on assistive chat; this preserves freshness but gives a meaningful hit-rate (~12-18%). - SLO posture: Leaning Option A (conservative) publicly; Option B as an internal sensitivity. We can call out Option B in the appendix with explicit tradeoffs. Attached: small note with utilization by service. -- Vivek Kulkarni VP, Infrastructure Redwood Inference [Attachment: util_by_service_note.txt (txt)] From: Karthik Iyer To: Neha Kapoor , Vivek Kulkarni , Lauren Bishop , Monica Patel Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 11:06:35 -0700 Subject: Re: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist Thanks — a few implementation caveats from Scheduling / Runtime side: - Spot vs Reserved: please break out a row in the model for preemption-sensitive vs tolerant workloads. For latency-critical routes we should avoid spot; for long-running embed jobs spot + retry is fine and materially lowers unit cost. - Preemption sensitivity: increasing batch size can worsen tail latency for preemptible workers if not paired with smarter eviction. We should add a small column showing 95th latency delta under batch=8 vs batch=1. I'll populate that by midday. - Model mix: I've added a new sheet (ModelMix) with token distribution assumptions (chat-heavy vs embed-heavy). If we shift 10% of traffic to small-parameter models for embedding-only workloads the cost delta is ~7% savings on core spend. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/QBR/2028/Capacity-Models/ModelMix (I updated the ModelMix tab in the v3 workbook) -Karthik Head of Serving Runtime From: Lauren Bishop To: Neha Kapoor , Vivek Kulkarni , Karthik Iyer , Monica Patel Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 13:28:00 -0700 Subject: Re: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist Appreciate the work here. High-level decisions for the QBR slides: 1) Public slide: present Option A (conservative posture) as our committed runway narrative. Call out Option B in the appendix as a "what we could realize with targeted batching + cache rollouts and a higher reserved mix." 2) Approve the batching/caching canary plan: implement batch=8 on top-5 non-rt routes for 10 business days, measure cost delta and 95th latency. If 95th increases < 200ms on average, expand to next tier. 3) Cost numbers: use Vivek's updated $2.18/hr reserved as the baseline in the deck. Monica — need a cost-sensitivity chart showing Base vs Optimistic vs Conservative with % savings and absolute $ delta for FY Q4. 4) Risk: keep the SLO risk-matrix graphic (slo-risk-matrix.png) on the slide; we'll call out the mitigation (canary + auto-fallback to lower batch). Finish this by EOD and drop slides in the QBR folder. Good trust exercise — let's surface the appendix with model assumptions. -Lauren Chief Product Officer Redwood Inference From: Neha Kapoor To: Lauren Bishop , Vivek Kulkarni , Karthik Iyer , Monica Patel Date: Fri, 25 Aug 2028 16:03:00 -0700 Subject: Re: QBR preflight: runway & capacity unit-econ checklist Thanks — summary and next steps: - Leadership decision: Option A public; Option B in appendix. Baseline reserved = $2.18/hr. - Canary: batch=8 on top-5 non-rt routes for 10 business days; TTL=45s for prefix cache on assistive flows. - Action items: * Monica: produce cost-sensitivity chart + slide (use revised $2.18 baseline) — deliverable: QBR slide deck appendix by EOD tomorrow. * Karthik: populate 95th-latency delta column for batch=8 vs batch=1 (by EOD today). * Vivek: finalize utilization per-service numbers and update the model (done) — please flag any outstanding pricing differences. * Me (Neha): I will merge annotated changes into qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx and finalize scenario tabs. Attachments referenced: [Attachment: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: batching_cache_experiments_summary.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: slo-risk-matrix.png (png)] I'll push the final workbook and the slide stub to the QBR folder once Karthik's latency column lands. Thanks everyone. Neha Kapoor Director, Infrastructure Planning Redwood Inference neha_kapoor@redwood.com
